subject: history
topicDisplay: World History Topics Two Same As Sl
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Wannsee Conference, which coordinated the 'Final Solution', was held in which year?
questions.explain: The Wannsee Conference of January 1942 coordinated the bureaucratic implementation of the systematic murder of Europe's Jews.

questions.q: Germany was admitted to the League of Nations in which year, a diplomatic success for Stresemann?
questions.explain: Germany joined the League of Nations in 1926, becoming a permanent member of the Council and signalling its return to the international community.

questions.q: The Reichstag Fire, which the Nazis exploited to suppress the Communists, took place in which month of 1933?
questions.explain: The Reichstag Fire of 27 February 1933 was blamed on the Communists and used to justify the Reichstag Fire Decree suspending civil liberties.

questions.q: What did the New Economic Policy (NEP) of 1921 permit?
options: Limited private trade and small business
questions.explain: The NEP allowed a tax in kind and limited private trade to revive the shattered economy.

questions.q: The Dawes Plan, which restructured German reparations and brought in US loans, was agreed in which year?
questions.explain: The Dawes Plan of 1924 rescheduled reparations and provided American loans, helping to stabilise the German economy.

questions.q: The 'Night of the Long Knives', the purge of the SA leadership and other rivals, occurred in which year?
questions.explain: In June-July 1934 Hitler purged the SA leadership, including Ernst Roehm, eliminating a perceived threat and winning army support.

questions.q: In which year did Nicholas II become Tsar?
questions.explain: Nicholas II succeeded his father Alexander III in 1894.

questions.q: The Locarno Treaties, marking a high point of Stresemann's foreign policy by guaranteeing Germany's western borders, were signed in which year?
questions.explain: The Locarno Treaties of 1925 confirmed Germany's western frontiers and improved relations, paving the way for League of Nations membership.

questions.q: In which year was Khrushchev removed from power?
questions.explain: Khrushchev was ousted by his Presidium colleagues in October 1964, ending the period studied.

questions.q: The Nazi leisure organisation offering workers holidays and activities was known by which name?
questions.explain: Kraft durch Freude (Strength Through Joy) provided subsidised leisure and travel to bind workers to the regime.

questions.q: What term described the forced merging of peasant farms from 1929?
questions.explain: Collectivisation forced peasants into kolkhozy, prompting resistance and famine.

questions.q: At which 1956 Congress did Khrushchev denounce Stalin's crimes?
questions.explain: Khrushchev's 'Secret Speech' attacking Stalin's cult of personality was delivered at the 20th Party Congress in 1956.

questions.q: What did the October Manifesto of 1905 promise?
options: A constitution and an elected Duma
questions.explain: The October Manifesto granted civil liberties and an elected State Duma, helping to defuse the 1905 Revolution.

questions.q: In which year was the Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany) established with its Basic Law?
questions.explain: The Federal Republic of Germany was founded in 1949 with the adoption of the Basic Law, with Konrad Adenauer as its first Chancellor.

questions.q: Which local self-government institutions did Alexander II establish in 1864?
questions.explain: The 1864 reform created elected zemstva, rural district and provincial councils responsible for local services.

questions.q: Konrad Adenauer, the first Chancellor of the Federal Republic, led which political party?
questions.explain: Adenauer led the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), serving as the first Chancellor of West Germany from 1949 to 1963.

questions.q: Hitler's failed attempt to seize power in Munich, the 'Beer Hall Putsch', took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Munich (Beer Hall) Putsch of November 1923 collapsed within hours, leading to Hitler's imprisonment, during which he wrote Mein Kampf.

questions.q: Which war's defeats helped spark unrest in 1905?
questions.explain: Humiliating defeats in the Russo-Japanese War of 1904-05 fuelled discontent leading to revolution.

questions.q: The nationwide anti-Jewish pogrom known as Kristallnacht ('Night of Broken Glass') took place in which year?
questions.explain: Kristallnacht occurred on 9-10 November 1938, with synagogues burned, Jewish businesses destroyed and tens of thousands arrested.

questions.q: What was the harsh economic policy of the Civil War period called?
questions.explain: War Communism (1918-21) involved grain requisitioning and nationalisation to supply the Red Army.

questions.q: In which year did Alexander II issue the Emancipation Edict freeing the serfs?
questions.explain: The Emancipation of the Serfs was decreed in February 1861, freeing roughly 23 million privately owned serfs.

questions.q: The Weimar Republic's constitution, which established a federal democratic state, was adopted in which year?
questions.explain: The Weimar Constitution was adopted in August 1919, creating a parliamentary democracy with a directly elected President.

questions.q: Stolypin's agrarian reforms after 1906 aimed to create what?
options: A class of prosperous independent peasants
questions.explain: Stolypin sought to break up the commune and foster a wealthy, loyal peasant class (his 'wager on the strong').

questions.q: Which 1942-43 battle marked the turning point on the Eastern Front?
questions.explain: The Battle of Stalingrad (1942-43) ended in a decisive Soviet victory and turned the war.

questions.q: The Enabling Act, which allowed Hitler's government to pass laws without the Reichstag, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The Enabling Act of March 1933 gave Hitler dictatorial powers to legislate without parliamentary or presidential approval for four years.

questions.q: The Wall Street Crash, which precipitated the Depression that devastated Germany, occurred in which year?
questions.explain: The Wall Street Crash of October 1929 caused American loans to be recalled, plunging Germany into mass unemployment and economic crisis.

questions.q: Hjalmar Schacht's 'New Plan' to control imports and stabilise the economy was introduced in which year?
questions.explain: Schacht's New Plan of 1934 regulated trade and foreign exchange to reduce Germany's trade deficit and fund rearmament.

questions.q: Which financial obligation bound former serfs to the state for decades after 1861?
questions.explain: Freed serfs had to make redemption payments, originally spread over 49 years, to compensate landowners for land allotments.

questions.q: The Young Plan, which further reduced and rescheduled Germany's reparations payments, was introduced in which year?
questions.explain: The Young Plan of 1929 reduced the total reparations bill and extended the repayment period, though it provoked nationalist opposition.

questions.q: Which 1918 treaty took Russia out of World War I?
questions.explain: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (March 1918) ended Russian participation in WWI at great territorial cost.
